https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/clyl.text: Image source, LightRocket via Getty Image Image caption, Mount Ololokwe in central Kenya is in a wildlife reserve By Basillioh Rukanga Â and Â Thomas Mukhwana ,Â Reporting from in Nairobi Published 19 August 2026, 12:32 BST Updated 28 minutes ago A helicopter has crashed in central Kenya at Mount Ololokwe in Samburu county, killing all six people on board, air accident officials have told the BBC. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Department said the identities of those on board were yet to be confirmed. Local media is reporting that the helicopter was carrying tourists. The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA) said the accident happened at approximately 09:13 local time (06:13 GMT). It said the helicopter was on a scenic flight from a wildlife conservancy in Losaiba to Ewaso Nyiro, a river that flows along several national reserves. An image shared online shows smoke as the crash site at Mount Ololokwe. The Kenya Red Cross has told the BBC that the area is not yet accessible, but drones are being used to assess the scene. The KCAA said the accident involved a Eurocopter EC130 B4 and it said it was co-ordinating operations. The transport ministry and Air Accident Investigations Department would lead "investigations into the circumstances surrounding the accident", it added. Helicopter crashes are not uncommon in Kenya. In February, a helicopter crash in the Rift Valley county of Nandi killed six people, including a member of parliament. In 2024, the military chief, Gen Francis Omondi Ogolla, died after an army helicopter that was carrying 11 people crashed in the west of the country, with only two survivors. In June 2021 at least 10 soldiers were killed when their helicopter crashed while landing near the capital, Nairobi. It comes during the final week in which Romania can still hit its remaining targets under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan agreed with the European Commission. Senators are debating the Hydrogen Law under emergency procedure, a crucial milestone without which the country risks losing a 2.84-billion-Euro payout. In parallel, deputies must re-examine the Integrity Law, modified following objections by the Constitutional Court, alongside new rules for high school entrance exams. Meanwhile, the adoption of the new public sector salary law remains uncertain, another major milestone on which 770 million Euro depend. Although the deadline is August 31st, the draft is still being analyzed by political parties following discussions with President Nicușor Dan. So far, only the Liberals have backed the latest version of the proposal, which faces fierce contestation from trade unions. New measures to restart the Cernavodă NPP Romanian authorities are taking new emergency measures to restart the nuclear power plant at Cernavodă, located in the southeast of the country along the Danube. The Ministry of Energy and Hidroelectrica are working to increase the river’s flow to ensure the water necessary for cooling the reactors. At the entry point into the country at Baziaș, in the southwest, the Danube’s flow is three times lower than the normal average for this period, measuring just 1,300 cubic meters per second compared to the usual 3,900. Under these conditions, the National Committee for Emergency Situations has already begun releasing large volumes of water from reservoirs along the Olt River. In addition, dredging operations continue. Although Cernavodă has backup deep wells, operating the nuclear reactors at maximum capacity depends on the high flow rate that only the Danube can supply. Currently, Romania is importing electricity daily at high prices. Romania reports highest EU fuel price spike Data from Eurostat shows Romania recorded the highest fuel price increase in the European Union over the past 12 months. The largest rate spikes for gasoline and diesel were registered in Romania at 24%, followed by Germany, Lithuania, and Bulgaria at around 22%. At the opposite end, the smallest price increases were recorded in Sweden at 1.2% and Ireland at 3%. The only country where prices dropped year-over-year in July 2026 compared to July 2025 was Hungary, with a slight dip of 0.1%. Looking at month-on-month figures for Romania, Eurostat notes diesel prices rose in July by 4.6% compared to June, while gasoline prices fell by 0.8%. Middle East peace talks In international news, interim Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu has strongly criticized recent statements made by Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, declaring them “completely unacceptable” on the X platform. Responding to the far-right Tel Aviv minister’s comments that Israel should kill 30 or 40 people every night in Gaza, Țoiu wrote: “It is not the first time we must speak out firmly, both in Romania and across the international community, to reaffirm that such statements contradict the painful lessons history has taught us regarding the immense dangers of dehumanization and calls to violence. These provocative calls for unjustifiable violence undermine efforts to obtain a peaceful solution, both by regional actors and internationally.” She emphasized that respect for human rights remains a foundational principle of Romanian foreign policy, firmly rejecting such dangerous rhetoric. The Foreign Minister reiterated Romania’s support for a two-state solution and added that under international law, Jewish settlements in the West Bank remain illegal, with violent actions there lacking any justification. Over 2.9 million Palestinians live in the West Bank, which is separated from Gaza by Israeli territory, alongside roughly 490,000 Israelis living in settlements considered illegal under international law. George Enescu competition kicks off Turning to culture, the 2026 George Enescu International Competition opens this Sunday at the Romanian Athenaeum. The opening concert features the Radio National Orchestra alongside the three winners of the 2024 edition: violinist Mayumi Kanagawa, cellist Yo Kitamura, and pianist Roman Lopatynskyi, under the baton of Maestro Cristian Măcelaru. The evening opens with The Stone and the Ivy , composed by Diego Santamaria—winner of the Originality Prize at the 2024 edition. Organizers note that including this piece reaffirms the competition’s commitment to contemporary creation and supporting new voices in music today. A major highlight of the evening will be the performance of Brahmsodia – Triple Concerto for Violin, Cello, Piano, and Orchestra Opus 169 , by Dan Dediu, one of the premier figures in contemporary Romanian music. Running from August 23 rd through September 19 th , the competition gathers young musicians from around the world to compete in violin, cello, piano, and composition. The event takes place under the High Patronage of the President of Romania, with Radio Romania serving as media partner. Fiery return leg for Universitatea Craiova In sports, Romanian football champion Universitatea Craiova from the south of the country is preparing for Thursday evening’s decisive away return match against Ararat-Armenia Yerevan in the Europa League play-offs. Following a 1-1 draw in the first leg at home in Craiova, Universitatea stands as Romania’s last remaining representative in European club competitions this season. The nation’s other three contenders, Universitatea Cluj and CFR Cluj from the northwest, as well as FCSB from Bucharest, were all eliminated in the preliminary rounds. https://aa.com.tr/en/world/morning-brief.text: World Morning Briefing: Sept. 7, 2026 Anadolu’s recap of top stories from around the globe Seyit Kurt 07 September 2026 • Update : 07 September 2026 ISTANBUL Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Monday, including Germany’s AfD party heading for a record victory in Saxony-Anhalt state, Israeli airstrikes killing at least seven people in southern Lebanon, and the US saying it sees progress toward a diplomatic resolution of the Ukraine conflict. TOP STORIES Germany's AfD projected to win Saxony-Anhalt election with record 44% vote Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) party is projected to win Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt with a record 44% of the vote, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservative Christian Democratic Union is set to slump to a historic low of 17.4%, according to projections with nearly 97% of the ballots counted. The remaining votes are not expected to change the outcome. The AfD would more than double its 20.8% result from 2021 and post its strongest showing in any German state election. Projections show the party falling short of a majority in the 83-seat parliament in Magdeburg and unable to govern alone. With all other major parties ruling out a coalition with the AfD, the result pointed to political uncertainty and long talks on forming a government. “We have achieved exactly what we set out to achieve. We have made history in this country,” AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund told public television. 7 killed, over 20 injured in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon despite US deal At least seven people were killed and more than 20 injured in Israeli airstrikes on several areas of southern Lebanon, Lebanese official sources said, as Israel continued daily violations of a US-brokered framework agreement. In the latest attacks, Al-Manar correspondent Ali Shbib and an accompanying cameraman whose name was not disclosed were injured in an Israeli strike targeting the city of Nabatieh, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported. The Health Ministry’s Emergency Operations Center said two people were killed and two injured in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, while eight people, including a woman and a girl, were injured in Nabatieh’s Al-Rahibat neighborhood. In Arab Salim, two women were killed and six people, including two girls, were injured, while four women were wounded in Kfar Remman, the ministry said. US envoy Witkoff says Washington sees progress on Ukraine peace US special envoy Steve Witkoff said Washington sees progress toward a diplomatic resolution of the Ukraine conflict and hopes to revive trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US. Speaking at a news conference in Kyiv alongside another US envoy, Jared Kushner, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Witkoff said the US team had brought ideas discussed with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow to Kyiv for further consideration. “We think we made a lot of progress in Moscow. We heard new ideas,” he said. Witkoff said the next step could include a trilateral meeting, adding the US believed cooperation between the parties was critical and that such a meeting would be announced soon. NEWS IN BRIEF US envoy Jared Kushner described the Israeli government as "a little irrational" regarding Gaza due to domestic political pressure ahead of upcoming elections. US President Donald Trump shared a photo in which the word "Mexico" in the New Mexico state name appeared to be crossed out and replaced with "America." An Amazon cargo plane caught fire and struck multiple vehicles after overrunning a runway at Miami International Airport in the US state of Florida, prompting over 60 fire rescue units to respond and shutting down all airport operations. The death toll from the sinking of a passenger vessel off the coast of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) rose to 14 after search and rescue teams recovered another body during ongoing operations, according to Turkish naval authorities. US Sen. Adam Schiff condemned anti-Muslim remarks made at a Jewish-American summit in Los Angeles, calling Muslim Americans an essential part of the nation. The Czech Republic is ready to support possible restrictions on the movement of Russian diplomats if such measures are coordinated with allies, Prime Minister Andrej Babis said. The Trump administration has made a third appeal to the US Supreme Court seeking to revive new rules governing mail-in ballots for the November midterm elections. Belgium's asylum and migration minister said she opposes allowing 13 Palestinian students from Gaza to enter Belgium despite having scholarships and visas to study in the country. Yemeni government forces launched a military operation against the Houthis to retake the Al-Kadha area and a road linking the cities of Taiz and Mokha in western Yemen, according to a government official. The death toll from devastating flash floods in Nepal reached 1,342, with thousands still missing, officials and local media reports said. Israeli Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir warned that Israel is facing a “tense and volatile period across all sectors” as the military continues its attacks on several regional fronts. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov called accusations against Russia over a drone incident at Germany's Leipzig Airport “the beginning of a real war.” Elements of the understandings reached in Anchorage “will always remain on the agenda,” Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said. US forces have redirected 92 commercial vessels while enforcing a maritime blockade against Iran, the US military's Central Command said. The Israeli army said it will launch a large-scale military exercise in the Red Sea city of Eilat and the Arava Valley along the Jordanian border on Monday to simulate a surprise attack. The foreign ministers of Türkiye, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates strongly condemned recent statements by Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Defense Minister Israel Katz regarding the displacement of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip. BUSINESS & ECONOMY Trump criticizes Canadian dollar 'imbalance' as trade tensions intensify US President Donald Trump criticized the alleged exchange-rate gap between the Canadian and US dollars, calling the "imbalance" unacceptable. "Canada's (currency) Dollar imbalance with the US is unacceptable," Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social. "It has been that way for years - but no longer!" He did not elaborate on what he meant by the remark. The Canadian dollar has historically been weaker than its US counterpart for most of the past 15 years. The long-term average stands at about $1 to 1.24 Canadian dollars. Since 2015, the currency has mostly traded between 1.20 Canadian dollars and 1.45 Canadian dollars against the greenback. It only reached or exceeded parity during part of the 2007-2012 commodity boom, when the Canadian dollar was stronger than the US dollar. The US dollar currently trades at around 1.38 Canadian dollars, meaning one Canadian dollar is worth roughly 72 US cents. Iran establishes ‘economic war headquarters’ amid US conflict, sanctions Iran’s Economy Ministry has established an “economic war headquarters” to coordinate and accelerate responses to economic problems arising from wartime conditions, Deputy Economy Minister Morteza Zamanian said. Zamanian told Tasnim news agency that the body would initially focus on issues falling within the ministry’s responsibilities and authorities. He said it would seek to quickly address war-related problems affecting businesses, trade, financing and other areas of the economy. SPORTS Türkiye retain European women's volleyball title with 3-2 win over Italy Türkiye retained their European women's volleyball title after defeating reigning world and Olympic champions Italy 3-2 in a five-set CEV EuroVolley Women final in Istanbul. Italy started strongly, with the opening set tied at 6-6 before taking an 11-8 lead and forcing Türkiye to call a timeout. Türkiye closed out the deciding set 15-10 to complete the 3-2 victory and claim back-to-back European titles. https://www.theguardian.com/politics/liv.text: Good morning. Ed Davey became Lib Dem leader in 2020, which means he is technically the longest-serving leader of a national party in the UK. (“Technically” because, while Nigel Farage only became leader of Reform UK in his current incumbency in 2024, he had led it before when it was called the Brexit party and, if you include Ukip, he has been leader of the anti-migrant, anti-EU right in British politics for more than 20 years.) After six years in charge, it is inevitable that some Lib Dems are starting to complain and, with the Lib Dem conference taking place in Brighton, Davey has been giving interviews this morning where he has had to respond to complaints from his critics. The most vocal has been Julian Brazil, the leader of Devon county council, who told the BBC yesterday that the Lib Dems were “sleepwalking into irrelevance” with Davey at the helm.
